title: Opening at ang 1
tomorrow: what are the very first words on that first page?

lines: THE FIRST PAGE OF A NEW NOTEBOOK.
WHERE THE GURU STARTS: ANG ONE.
cards: A brand-new notebook does something strange to people. Some skip the first page, scared to spoil it. Some tear it out after one bad line.
A book as big as the Granth makes those nerves louder. So where does anyone start? The plain answer is the best one: where the Guru starts.

teach.h: ANG: A PAGE, AND A LIMB.
teach.b: Ang is the word Sikhs use for a page of the Granth. It also means a limb, a part of a body, and some readers say that fits a book treated as a living Guru. Now feel the opening the way a reader does.
Hands washed, head covered. The rumala, the cloth over the book, folded back. The pages turned to the front.
And the first thing the eyes meet isn't a sentence. At the top of ang one is a single sign, Ik Onkar, and it begins with the numeral one.

teach.h: BEFORE A WORD, THE NUMBER ONE.
teach.b: Something to tell someone tonight: the Granth opens on a number before it opens on a word. Why start there, and not at a favorite hymn? A daily hukamnama opens wherever the book falls.
A favorite hymn is easy to find.

But a full reading that begins at ang one meets everything in the Guru's own order: the daily prayers first, then the ragas, the hard pages with the loved ones. Nothing gets skipped because it's unfamiliar.
The weeks ahead walk that order, page by page.

how: A full reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, whether a sehaj path at home or a reading in the gurdwara, begins at ang 1 with the Japji; the book is opened with washed hands and a covered head, its cloth folded back.

practice: If you have a gutka or the Granth on a screen, open it to the very first page slowly, as if folding back a cloth, and let your eyes rest on the first sign before any words.
If not, trace the shape of the number one in the air with a finger, slowly, top to bottom. Breathe while you trace it, and let one be all you hold.

wordCard.voice: Opening at ang 1. Starting a reading where the Guru starts: the first page, the first sign, the number one. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: ang, a limb or part of a body; the word for a page of the Guru Granth Sahib.

carryVoice: Keep this: begin at the beginning, and let the Guru set the order of the pages. Rest well.
